Let me analyze each user story:

U1: NIO stack toggle via deploy.properties + WebSocket components in flows
U2: Registry pairing via registry key, HTTP endpoint management
U3: Dynamic lookup component for flows (supports Registry Dynamic Endpoint Resolution)
U4: Throttling policies for Mule ESB flow endpoints (Registry user)
U5: Custom business events and transaction IDs printed to logs during development
U6: Upgrade MVEL dependency to 2.1.8 (used for DataMapper and MVEL)
U7: JDBC connectivity for popular relational databases (Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, DB2, MySQL done)

5. Throttling policies will integrate with existing policy framework

8. JDBC connectivity will use existing JDBC transport/connectors

technical_and_design_decisions: Mule ESB is Java-based; all development will use Java 7/8 compatible with Mule 3.5.0.
NIO stack toggle will be implemented via a property in deploy.properties that switches the underlying transport implementation for HTTP/TCP connectors.

WebSocket components will be built as new Mule transports following the existing transport SPI, supporting both server and client endpoints, and will integrate with the Mule flow model via message processors.
Registry pairing will use a registry key configured in deploy.properties or mule-config.xml; a registry client will handle authentication, endpoint registration, and periodic heartbeats via REST API.
Dynamic lookup component will be a new router that resolves endpoints at runtime by querying the Registry, with caching and fallback mechanisms.

Throttling policies will be enforced via an interceptor in the HTTP inbound endpoint chain, retrieving policy definitions from the Registry and applying rate-limiting algorithms (token bucket, fixed window).
Business event and transaction ID logging will extend Mule's logging framework (log4j) with custom appenders and MDC propagation, configurable via log4j.properties.
MVEL dependency will be upgraded to 2.1.8 in the project POM; DataMapper and MVEL expression language usage will be regression tested.
JDBC connectivity for each database will reuse the existing JDBC transport, adding database-specific dialect classes for SQL generation, connection pool tuning, and driver management.

Query logging in DEBUG mode will be implemented via a JDBC proxy wrapper (using java.sql.Wrapper or a proxy library) that intercepts execute/query calls and logs SQL with parameters when DEBUG is enabled.
assumptions: Existing Mule 3.5.0 codebase, build system (Maven), and test infrastructure are available and familiar to the developer.
Registry API is stable, documented, and accessible; the wiki link provides sufficient detail for integration.
WebSocket implementation will follow JSR-356 (Java API for WebSocket) or equivalent standard.
NIO stack toggle affects only HTTP and TCP transports; other transports remain unchanged.
Throttling policies are defined in the Registry and pushed to the ESB instance; the ESB does not persist policies locally beyond caching.
Dynamic lookup component will be used in flows as a routing element; it does not replace existing static endpoint configuration.
Database drivers for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, and DB2 are available in Maven Central or corporate repository.
MySQL JDBC support is already complete and tested.
Query logging can be implemented without significant performance overhead when disabled (DEBUG level off).
Single developer performs all work; no parallelization across team members.
Effort estimates include unit testing, integration testing, and basic documentation but exclude extensive performance tuning or user acceptance testing.
Code reviews are self-performed; no formal peer review process.
A buffer of 5 workdays is included for unforeseen bugs and integration issues.

activities.activity_description: Design the deploy.properties toggle for enabling NIO stack, including property naming, default values, and impact on transport selection.
Add parsing of the NIO toggle property in the configuration bootstrap and propagate to transport factories.
Refactor HTTP and TCP transport implementations to conditionally use NIO-based connectors (e.g., Netty or JDK NIO) when toggle is enabled.
Define WebSocket transport SPI, message processors, endpoint builders, and integration points with Mule flow model.
Develop inbound WebSocket endpoint supporting handshake, message framing, and session management.
Develop outbound WebSocket endpoint for connecting to remote WebSocket servers, including reconnection logic.
Wire WebSocket endpoints into flow construction, support transformers, filters, and exception strategies.
Provide built-in transformers for WebSocket frames (text/binary) and filters for message routing.
Write unit tests verifying NIO toggle parsing and transport selection logic.
Unit test WebSocket server/client endpoints, transformers, and error handling.

activities.activity_name: Integration tests for WebSocket in flows
activities.activity_description: End-to-end tests of WebSocket endpoints within Mule flows, including clustering and load scenarios.
Define configuration schema for registry key in deploy.properties and mule-config.xml, with validation.
Develop HTTP client for Registry API: authentication, pairing, endpoint registration, deregistration, and heartbeat.
Hook into application deployment lifecycle to register HTTP endpoints with the Registry.
Hook into application undeployment lifecycle to remove endpoints from Registry.
Schedule periodic status updates to Registry to maintain pairing and detect instance health.
Implement retry logic, circuit breaker, and local caching for Registry unavailability.
Validate registry key format, connectivity, and permissions at startup.
Unit test registry client with mock server, covering success and failure paths.
Integration tests using a mock Registry to verify endpoint registration, heartbeat, and failure handling.
Define router component that resolves endpoints dynamically via Registry at runtime.
Implement lookup logic: query Registry for endpoint metadata, construct endpoint URIs.
Add TTL-based cache to reduce Registry calls; handle cache invalidation.
Define fallback behavior when Registry is unreachable or endpoint not found (e.g., use static config, throw exception).
Register dynamic lookup as a router, support in flow XML and annotation configuration.
Unit test resolution, caching, fallback with mocked Registry.
End-to-end test of dynamic lookup in a flow with real Registry interaction.
Define policy data model (rate limits, quotas, algorithms) and how policies are associated with endpoints via Registry.
Create interceptor for HTTP inbound endpoints that evaluates throttling policies per request.

activities.activity_name: Integrate with Registry for policy retrieval
activities.activity_description: Fetch throttling policies from Registry at startup and on change notifications; cache locally.
Evaluate request against policy (token bucket, fixed window, sliding window); return 429 when exceeded.
Implement token bucket, fixed window, and sliding window algorithms; make algorithm configurable per policy.
Allow policy configuration (limits, algorithms) to be managed entirely in Registry UI.
Unit test interceptor, algorithms, and policy evaluation with mocked time and Registry.
Integration test with real HTTP endpoints and Registry policies under load.
Define extension points for custom business events and transaction ID propagation in Mule's event model.
Ensure transaction ID (correlation ID) is propagated across flow components, threads, and transports via MDC.
Provide API for developers to log custom business events with structured data (JSON) at key points in flows.
Hook into log4j configuration; add custom appenders/layouts for business events and transaction IDs.
Add log4j.properties entries to enable/disable business event logging and set output format.
Test transaction ID propagation, custom event API, and log output verification.
Review MVEL 2.1.8 release notes and changelog for breaking changes affecting DataMapper and expression language.
Modify project POM to use MVEL 2.1.8; resolve any transitive dependency conflicts.
Address any compilation errors due to API changes in MVEL 2.1.8.
Execute full DataMapper test suite to detect regressions.
Debug and fix any runtime failures or behavioral changes in DataMapper and MVEL expressions.
Benchmark expression evaluation performance before and after upgrade.
Update release notes and any developer guides referencing MVEL version.
Add Oracle driver dependency, implement Oracle dialect for SQL generation, configure connection pooling, test CRUD operations, document configuration.
Add PostgreSQL driver, implement dialect, connection pool tuning, test CRUD, document.
Add Sybase (jConnect) driver, implement dialect, test CRUD, document.
Add Microsoft JDBC driver, implement dialect, test CRUD, document.
Add DB2 driver, implement dialect, test CRUD, document.
Design a proxy/wrapper for java.sql.Connection/Statement/PreparedStatement to intercept query execution.
Implement proxy that logs SQL, parameters, and execution time at DEBUG level using log4j.

activities.activity_name: Integrate query logging with JDBC connector
activities.activity_description: Modify JDBC connector to optionally wrap connections with logging proxy when DEBUG enabled for query logger.
Ensure minimal overhead when DEBUG is off; use lazy logging and avoid string concatenation.
Add log4j logger category for JDBC queries and property to enable/disable.
Test proxy interception, parameter logging, and DEBUG level control.
End-to-end test with real databases verifying SQL appears in logs at DEBUG.
Update user guides, configuration references, and API docs for all new features.
Compile release notes summarizing new features, upgrades, and bug fixes.
Update Maven build profiles, CI pipelines for new dependencies and test suites.
Perform code reviews on own changes before commit.
Buffer for unforeseen bugs, integration issues, and regression fixes.
